- Most 429s for requests with concurrency > 50 and sustained bursts; many clients see one or two successful tokens then immediate throttling.
- We cannot tolerate repeated 429s; our SLAs are at risk.

We need immediate mitigation and a clear plan (root cause + timeline to permanent fix). Please escalate to the appropriate exec if needed — we need a rapid response and a temporary capacity/limit adjustment while you investigate.

Alex

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Production API 429s and latency spikes — Elantra (urgent)

Quick technical summary (initial triage):
- Root cause (likely): overlapping quota policies + an incorrectly set burst window for the tenant. We see two active quota rules affecting ELAN-4721: a route-level token bucket and a tenant-level bucket. Both are configured to draw from the same backing credits without proper harmonization.
- Misconfiguration detail: tenant-level burst_window_seconds is set to 60s (should be 3600s for this account profile). That short burst window causes the token bucket to exhaust quickly under sustained bursts; when combined with route-level enforcement we effectively double-throttle concurrent requests.
- Symptom match: requests process initial tokens (one or two) and then hit immediate 429s until the bucket refills — matches Alex's logs.

Immediate mitigation steps executed:
A) Increased tenant soft-limit by 2x for 60 minutes (we implemented per Rachel's ask).
B) Bumped tenant burst_window_seconds from 60 -> 3600 (hotfix applied to policy store and propagated to runtime); this requires bucket reindex to avoid leftover drained states.
C) Enabled fallback routing to rwd-embed-lite for the chat/read routes (traffic shifted ~22% to fallback during the peak).

Risks & follow-up:
- Reindex operation may cause minor transient latencies as buckets reconcile (estimated < 90s). We'll run it in a rolling fashion and monitor p95.
- Need a permanent policy harmonization: consolidate route-level and tenant-level quota rules, add unit tests and alerting on burst_window anomalies.
- Recommend an exec note to Prod Ops to authorize a one-time reserve buffer for large promotional spikes for customers with high concurrency.

I'll push a short incident note to the drive link and tag Monica for the customer message draft.

— Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Alex —

Update and next steps: thank you for the logs, they made triage much faster. In short: we identified a policy configuration drift where a tenant-level burst window was set to 60s (too short for your traffic profile) and combined with a route-level enforcement this produced double-throttling behavior during the promotional spike.

What we did (completed):
- Applied a temporary soft-limit uplift (2x) while we validated the fix (60 minutes window enacted at 08:36 PDT).
- Hotfixed tenant burst_window_seconds 60 -> 3600 and reindexed buckets (rolling, <90s transient).
- Enabled fallback routing to rwd-embed-lite to preserve throughput for read-heavy flows (shifted ~22% of traffic).

Impact: 429s dropped from ~15% to <1.5% within 12 minutes of mitigation; p95 latencies returned to baseline within the reindex window. We'll continue monitoring for 24 hours.

Permanent work:
- Policy harmonization and a safety buffer for promotional spikes (config + alerting).
- Add regression tests and a console alert on burst_window values outside expected ranges for large tenants.

Compensation: Marissa/Finance will propose a goodwill credit; suggested 10% for May usage as a starting point — I'll loop Procurement after you confirm.

Assigned lead: Monica Patel (CS) will coordinate follow-up and a post-incident writeup (drive link attached).

If you'd like to jump on a quick call to walk through the fixes and timeline, Monica and I are available now.

Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as high priority.
